newsitem.title: USA: Hartford Whalers hockey team to leave Connecticut.
newsitem.headline: Hartford Whalers hockey team to leave Connecticut.

text.p: The Hartford Whalers hockey team rejected Connecticut Governor John Rowland's proposal to build a $147 million arena and will leave the state at the end of this season, Rowland said on Wednesday.
Republican Rowland told a news conference that the National Hockey League team has agreed to pay the state an exit fee of $20.5 million.
"On Tuesday, Whalers owner Peter Karmanos rejected what I would refer to as the state's best offer," Rowland said. "Mr. Karmanos obviously believes that there's a better deal out there."
Rowland said Karmanos made it clear to him that the door was closed and that there was no chance of a last-minute solution. He did not say where the Whalers were headed.
Karmanos is expected to hold a news conference at 1300 EST.
The two sides had been negotiating over the team's future for several months.
Rowland said his proposal to build a $147 million "state of the art facility" would have generated revenues of more than $50 million a year for the Whalers.
"I believe we brought the state's position as far as we possibly could," he said.

"We've had a good run for the last 17 or 18 years," Rowland said. "(But) we've made a decision that's in the best interests of the Hartford community and the best interests of the taxpayers of this state."
Major sticking points included the Whalers' rejection of a long-term lease at the new facility, Rowland said.
Another problem was the team's projection it would lose at least $45 million during the three years while the arena was being built.
"Their request was that the state would assume that entire cost," Rowland said.

"So in addition to bonding a $147 million facility, they were requesting a cash payment of at least $45 million for the next three years, and then of course we would not have appropriate revenue to pay off our bonds," Rowland said.
"They wanted the facility rent-free. We had offered that they pay $2.5 million in rent, so that we could make an effort to make this revenue-neutral and to pay off the bonds."
The team also wanted no surcharges or taxes on tickets or luxury suites, and wanted all luxury suites sold or committed to by May 1, and sales of 13,000 season tickets by that date.
"Needless to say, that was an impossibility," Rowland said.
Rowland said Connecticut would try to lure a minor league hockey team to the Civic Center to replace the Whalers.
The Whalers were the state's only major league sports franchise.
"I don't believe the city of Hartford is going to be made or broken based on the Whalers," Rowland said, adding that downtown still had "wonderful cultural events."
Hartford Mayor Mike Peters said on local radio that losing the team was a setback. "We'll have to step back for a minute, take a deep breath, and see where we go from here."
